course.title: On-Call — Incident Command for Platform Engineers
course.summary: A 4-week cohort with a live game-day. You'll command a simulated outage, coordinate responders, communicate to stakeholders and write the postmortem.
course.subtitle: Run calm incidents, write blameless postmortems, ship reliability
course.description:
**Stay calm at 3 a.m.** On-Call is a four-week cohort for engineers who carry the pager, or are about to. You will learn to take command of an incident, coordinate responders, keep stakeholders informed and turn every outage into a better system. In week three you run a live game day: a simulated cascading failure in a sandbox cluster, graded on how you command it.

## Curriculum

| Module | Week | Formats |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Briefing | 1 | kickoff video, rules of engagement |
| 1. Signals | 1 | annotated dashboard, SLOs and error budgets, conference talk |
| 2. Command | 2 | SEV1 role-play video, bridge-call recording, branching scenario, printable runbook |
| 3. Game day | 3 | SCORM outage simulator, xAPI-tracked live drill, comms quiz |
| 4. After | 4 | blameless postmortems, postmortem assignment with peer and tutor review |

## Outcomes

- Declare and classify incidents with a shared severity matrix
- Run the first five minutes of a SEV1: roles, channel, first update
- Communicate impact, current action and next update time to any audience
- Alert on SLO burn rate instead of on causes
- Write a blameless postmortem with owned, dated action items

## Format

Four weeks, about 4–5 hours a week, plus a 90-minute live drill. Each cohort has at most 24 engineers, so every drill gets individual feedback. Deadlines are real: the comms quiz closes on Thursday of week 3, the postmortem is due at the end of week 4.

## Instructors

**Priya Raman** is a Staff SRE who has run the incident programme for a platform of 400 services, and wrote its runbook, severity matrix and postmortem template.

**Marek Lis** has been an incident commander at a fintech processing card payments in 30 countries. He runs the game day and grades the drills.

Complete all modules and pass the drill to earn **Incident Commander — Level 1**.

lessons.title: 0. Briefing
lessons.summary: Cohort welcome, schedule, grading and the rules everyone follows on the bridge.

topics.title: Course kickoff
topics.summary: Week 3 is the live game day. Deadlines: comms quiz Thursday of week 3, postmortem end of week 4.
topics.introduction: Cohort welcome, the four-week schedule and how drills are graded.
topics.description:
**Transcript**

PRIYA: Welcome to On-Call. Over four weeks you will learn to command an incident, not just to survive one.

MAREK: Week three is the game day. We break a sandbox cluster, you run the incident. We grade time to declare, the first stakeholder update, time to mitigate and your handover note.

PRIYA: Three rules for the whole cohort: mitigate before you debug; every message says impact, action and next update; and no blame. Ever.

topics.title: Rules of engagement
topics.summary: Declare high, downgrade fast. IC decides, comms talks, ops fixes, scribe writes it down.
topics.introduction: The severity matrix (SEV1–SEV4) and the four incident roles.

lessons.title: 1. Signals
lessons.summary: Read dashboards like an IC and alert on what users feel.

topics.title: Anatomy of an alert
topics.summary: Start with the symptom (B), rule out traffic (E), follow saturation (C) to the likely cause. Tail latency (D) moves before the median.
topics.introduction: An annotated dashboard from the moment checkout started failing.

topics.title: SLOs and error budgets
topics.summary: budget = (1 − SLO) × window: 99.9 % over 30 days is 43.2 minutes. Page on fast burn, ticket on slow burn.
topics.introduction: SLIs, SLOs, error budgets and burn-rate alerts, with worked examples.

topics.title: Talk: "Alert fatigue is a bug"
topics.summary: Every page should be urgent, actionable and about user impact. Everything else is a ticket or a dashboard.
topics.introduction: SREcon16 talk "Less Alarming Alerts!" on cutting alert noise. Watch it with your own alert list open.

lessons.title: 2. Command
lessons.summary: Take command, keep the bridge disciplined and decide under pressure.

topics.title: Taking command
topics.summary: Names and roles in every request, questions before theories, a time for the next checkpoint.
topics.introduction: Role-play of the first five minutes of a SEV1.

topics.title: Radio discipline
topics.summary: Mistakes: no IC declared, "can someone…" requests, two conversations at once, a guess in the public channel, no next-update time.
topics.introduction: A recorded incident bridge call. Listen, read the transcript and spot the five mistakes.
topics.description:
**Transcript (excerpt)**

`03:13` **Dev 1:** Is anyone looking at checkout? *(mistake 1: nobody takes command)*

`03:13` **Dev 2:** Can someone check the database? *(mistake 2: request with no name)*

`03:14` **Dev 3:** I'm restarting the pods… **Dev 1:** wait, I'm also looking at the load balancer *(mistake 3: two conversations, conflicting actions)*

`03:16` **Dev 2 in #general:** Probably Ben's deploy again *(mistake 4: guess and blame in public)*

`03:18` **Manager:** When will it be fixed? **Dev 1:** Soon. *(mistake 5: no impact, no next update time)*

**Rewrite one minute of this call** with roles, names and a next-update time, and bring it to the live session.

*The recording is a soundscape of a bridge line; the dialogue is in this transcript.*

topics.title: Who does what?
topics.introduction: A branching scenario: you are the IC of a SEV1. Every choice changes what happens next.

topics.title: Incident runbook template
topics.summary: Print it, fill in the contacts page for your team and keep it next to your laptop.
topics.introduction: A printable runbook: severity matrix, roles, the first five minutes, comms templates and a contacts page.

lessons.title: 3. Game day
lessons.summary: Command a simulated cascading failure, run the live drill and check your comms.

topics.title: Outage simulator
topics.summary: Score 70+ to pass. Your timeline from the simulator is the input for the postmortem in module 4.
topics.introduction: A simulated cascading failure with live metrics, a timeline and a chat pane. Keyboard: 1–9.

topics.title: Live drill
topics.summary: Tick each checkpoint as it happens; the timestamps go to your learning record and to your facilitator.
topics.introduction: The xAPI-tracked live drill in the sandbox cluster drill-eu-1. Thursday of week 3, 18:00 CET.

topics.title: Comms check
topics.introduction: Eight questions on incident communication. Two attempts, 15 minutes. Due Thursday of week 3.

lessons.title: 4. After
lessons.summary: Turn the outage into learning: blameless postmortem, review, reading.

topics.title: Blameless postmortems
topics.summary: Describe conditions, not culprits. Several contributing factors, several owned and dated action items.
topics.introduction: The template, the five whys used carefully, and contributing factors vs root cause.

topics.title: Postmortem assignment
topics.introduction: Write the postmortem for the game-day outage in Markdown or PDF. Peer and tutor review.

topics.title: Reading list
topics.introduction: Papers and books the cohort keeps coming back to.

course.target_group: SREs, platform/backend engineers joining on-call, engineering managers
